title: Exceptional transport object and functor data
statement: Given the finite and integral operation families and compact-support left realizations of the exceptional ring construction, there exists TransportCoreData with the reconstruction, operation, functor, adjunction, left-comparison, evaluation, and integral-left-realization fields. Its right comparison realizeG is not an independent field: for every E it is the inverse of Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq from the reconstructed system adjunction transported on the left by realizeF inverse to the given integral operation adjunction. Thus realizeG is explicitly determined by the two adjunctions and realizeF, without an additional compatibility hypothesis. The reduction comparisons reductionF and reductionG are likewise not independent fields: they are defined from realizeF and realizeG by whiskering through the target reconstruction functor and composing with its counit isomorphism and the right unitor.

source.place: Constructions 4.1 and 5.25, Lemma 5.22 and Propositions 5.24 and 5.26

proof.text: Choose the reconstruction and shift package from the isolated reconstruction subproblem. Choose coherent integral operations and realizations from the integral compactification realization theorem. Apply the isolated transported functor/comparison package and assemble the independent fields of TransportCoreData, omitting the former arbitrary realizeG, reductionF and reductionG fields. Define reductionF and reductionG from realizeF and realizeG by whiskering through the target reconstruction functor and composing with its counit isomorphism and the right unitor; do not choose the two reduction comparisons independently.

Define TransportCoreData.realizeG by the inverse of rightAdjointUniq for the reconstructed adjunction, transported along realizeF inverse, and the integral operation adjunction. Both left adjoints coincide. This is the explicit unit/counit construction of the uniqueness isomorphism, not a witness chosen from an unproved existence statement.

theorem exists_exceptional_transport_core_data
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω]
    [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω] (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification f)
    (operation : ∀ s : RingStage.{u} l, Operation.{u} l Ω X Y (s.stage l))
    (left : ∀ s : RingStage.{u} l,
      LeftRealization.{u} l Ω c s (operation s)) :
    Nonempty (TransportCoreData l Ω D hl c operation left)

statement_change.what: The previous data record allowed an arbitrary realizeG although every consumer requires the specified adjunction-compatible comparison. On an identity adjunction in characteristic zero, a minus-identity comparison changes the transported adjunction. Replace this free data field by the explicit uniqueness construction, not by a new law hypothesis. The data existence theorem and final Transported interface keep their written signatures.
